name: felix-doc-auditor-pre-rework

subject.implementation: OpenClaw-mediated agent (current production path; to be retired in WP09)
subject.invocation: openclaw cron tick -> agent execution per scripts/openclaw/agents/felix-doc-auditor/AGENTS.md

measurements.description: Tick exits cleanly with no audits to process (queue blocked on pending decisions, or no new audits).

representative_samples.note: Median empty tick — short clean exit, 3 LLM calls.
High-cost empty tick — agent re-read context across multiple files this hour.

measurements.description: Tick processed an audit and produced one or more docs-debt issues without applying a code edit.
Tick processed an audit that produced a Tier-A auto-commit (typically a frontmatter `last_validated` bump) plus follow-up actions.

samples.verified_tier_a_commit: fa50fc61 chore(doc-audit): [tier-a] bump last_validated on docs/INDEX.md (audit: #329)

samples.note: Heuristic classifier placed this tick in tier_a_apply; manual inspection shows it was actually a post-validation 'empty audit' for the audit auto-filed by tick-0002's commit. Cost shape (heavy read, light apply) is intermediate between empty and true tier_a — retained here for now; see open_caveats.

summary_for_nfr_001.comment: Weighted by observed mix (28 empty / 4 debt_only / 2 tier_a_apply). Mix bias toward 'empty' reflects a stretch of blocked-queue ticks during the measurement window. For NFR-001 we hold the per-outcome averages as the comparator (post-rework values must each be <=20% of these to satisfy >=80% reduction).

methodology.summary: OpenClaw writes a per-agent session JSONL containing every cron-tick user message and the assistant responses with token usage in a `usage` field on each assistant record. We tokenize the JSONL into per-tick groups (boundary: user message matching the cron-tick preamble), sum the per-call usage fields, and aggregate by tick outcome.
methodology.usage_field_shape: Each assistant message has a `message.usage` object with integer fields `input`, `output`, `cacheRead`, `cacheWrite` and a `totalTokens` denormalization. We treat `total_input_tokens_billable = input + cacheRead + cacheWrite` to mirror Anthropic's billing model (cache-read and cache-write tokens are charged at different per-token rates but all consume the input-side quota).
methodology.outcome_classification: Heuristic regex match against the closing assistant text of each tick. Patterns (in priority order): tier_a_apply (Tier-A keyword OR `committed` OR short SHA reference); debt_only (debt-issue keyword); empty (NO_REPLY / no work / clean exit). Outcome label may need manual correction for edge cases — see open_caveats.
reproduction_steps: 2. Identify the active agent session: `ls -la /home/claude/.openclaw/agents/felix-doc-auditor/sessions/`. Pick the largest active jsonl (excluding .bak files).
3. SCP `scripts/doc_audit/baselines/measure-tokens.py` to office2 (or run from the deployed `/data/services/openclaw/...` copy).
5. Inspect classifications: `python3 -c "import json; [print(o['outcome'], o['sample_count']) for o in json.load(open('/tmp/per-outcome.json'))['by_outcome']]"`.
6. Spot-check at least one sample per outcome by reading the closing assistant text via `--per-tick --from-tick N --to-tick N`. Correct outcome labels in the emitted JSON if heuristic misfired.

7. Promote into baseline JSON: copy per-outcome averages + representative samples into `docs/design/architecture/baselines/felix-doc-auditor-pre-rework.json` (or `<service>-post-rework.json` for WP09).
methodology.sample_size_guidance: Target >=3 samples per outcome over a 3-day natural-traffic window. If a Tier-A outcome doesn't appear naturally, an operator-driven synthetic audit (file a low-stakes Doc audit issue against a doc whose `last_validated` is stale by >=30 days) is acceptable; document the synthetic origin in the sample note.
methodology.future_use: WP09 (post-rework cutover) reuses this same script + methodology against the new driver's session log (or its activity log / tick-signal records) to produce `felix-doc-auditor-post-rework.json`. NFR-001 acceptance is per-outcome: post-rework `average_total_input_tokens_billable` must be <=20% of the pre-rework value for at least the `empty` outcome (the high-volume case), and operator-acceptable for `debt_only` and `tier_a_apply`.

open_caveats: Mix bias: 28 of 34 ticks observed were `empty` because the audit queue was blocked on two pending-approval issues (#302, #318) throughout the measurement window. Re-baselining during a more active period would shift the mix; per-outcome averages are robust to this but the `weighted_average_*` numbers are not.

Heuristic outcome classifier is approximate. Tick-0003 was tagged `tier_a_apply` by the heuristic but manual inspection shows it was actually a post-validation 'empty audit' of the prior tick's Tier-A commit. Token cost is intermediate; we left the auto-classification in place and noted it in the sample for transparency. For WP09 (post-rework) re-measurement, an operator should spot-check classifications.

OpenClaw's session JSONL accumulates context across ticks (cache_read grows over time as more turns accumulate). The first few ticks of a fresh session pay a large `cache_write` cost that subsequent ticks recoup; longer-running sessions show a more stable `cache_read`-dominated profile. The 33-hour window here covers both phases.

No per-LLM-call attribution. The session JSONL emits one `usage` record per assistant turn, not per logical operation (tier_classification, debt_body_generation, cross_file_implication). The new driver in WP05 emits separate counts (`judgment.tier_classification_calls` etc.) in `last-tick.json`, which is what the post-rework measurement will consume.
Excluded: any LLM traffic NOT routed through OpenClaw (e.g., manual `gh` debugging by the operator). The session JSONL is OpenClaw-only, so this measurement reflects only the agent's autonomous work.
